newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 26.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 26.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Wednesday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:
** India on Tuesday gave its economy mixed grades and said more free-market reforms were needed to compete with developing powerhouses like China.
In an annual report on the state of the economy, the
centre-left government said a liberalisation programme launched in 1991 had placed India, with seven percent average annual growth, among the top 10 economic performers in the world.
But, the future is clouded by infrastructure
bottlenecks, rising inflation and sluggish exports, it said in the Economic Survey for the 1996/97 fiscal year ending on March 31.
** The government on Tuesday forecast industrial growth of about 10 percent for 1996/97 (April-March) compared to 11.7 percent in 1995/96.
"A better agricultural performance in the second half of
the year is likely to result in increased demand that augurs well for the industry," it said in the Survey.
** The government said that it remains committed to reducing the fiscal deficit as a share of gross domestic product (GDP).
The survey did not give an estimate of the 1996/97
fiscal deficit as a share of GDP. It repeated the target which the government set last year of 5.0 percent of GDP, down from 5.8 percent in 1995/96.
** The Survey said the deficit on the oil pool account is expected to rise to 155 billion rupees in 1996/97 compared to 57 billion in the previous fiscal year.
The oil pool deficit is effectively the amount the
government owes state oil companies for selling oil products to Indian consumers below world prices.
MARKETS:
** The Indian rupee opened at 35.875/880 against the dollar on Wednesday compared to the previous close of 35.865/875, dealers said.
Wednesday's range seen at 35.86/88 rupees to a dollar,
they said.
** Shares at major Indian bourses ended Tuesday near the day's lowest levels and hardly changed from the previous close which indicated a weak undertone, dealers said.
The Bombay Stock Exchange's benchmark 30-share index
ended 1.645 points, or 0.05 percent, lower at 3,356.83.
** The 50-stock National Stock Exchange index edged up 3.40 points, or 1.35 percent, to 966.10.
** The Delhi share index .DE rose 8.47 points to 727.02.
** The Calcutta share index .CALSN climbed 0.44 points to 440.95.
** The Madras share index .MDSI added 30.77 points to 3,352.67.
